# Chicago Cosplay Weekend Plan for 2

A low-stress, budget-aware convention plan for **2 people** in Chicago from **2026-07-10 to 2026-07-12**. I’m assuming you want a **fictional fan convention near downtown/Loop or McCormick Place**, with **costumes, snacks, and local transit only** covered by the **$320 total**.

## Budget, Cosplay Picks, and Daily Flow

| Category | Plan | Estimated Cost |
|---|---|---:|
| Easy cosplay | **Traveler / adventurer** using closet pieces + one prop | **$55** |
| Detailed cosplay | **Anime hero / game character-inspired build** with wig, foam, paint, accessories | **$115** |
| Snacks | Water, electrolyte drinks, fruit, granola, sandwiches, treats | **$70** |
| Local transit | CTA rides / occasional rideshare buffer | **$40** |
| Backup buffer | Safety pins, tape, glue, emergency replacement item | **$40** |
| Total |  | **$320** |

## Ranked Cosplay Plan

Option 1: **Easy cosplay — Traveler / adventurer** | Fast, comfortable, convention-friendly | **Best for all-day wear**
Action: [Button: Build this look](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=cosplay+accessories+travel+cloak)

Option 2: **More detailed cosplay — Hero / mage / ranger build** | More visual impact, still manageable in a weekend | **Best for photos and panels**
Action: [Button: Shop supplies](https://www.michaels.com/)

Option 3: **Backup cosplay tweak — themed variant of your main outfit** | Lets both people stay coordinated without doubling work | **Best for budget control**
Action: [Button: Get ideas](https://www.pinterest.com/)

### Easy cosplay: Traveler / adventurer
- Base pieces: neutral pants, boots/sneakers, plain shirt, belt, light jacket or vest
- Add-ons: small pouch, scarf, fingerless gloves, cardboard/foam prop
- Why it works: comfortable, cheap, and easy to sit, eat, and walk in

### Detailed cosplay: Hero / mage / ranger build
- Base pieces: thrifted layers, long coat or tunic, boots, gloves
- Build pieces: EVA foam shoulder piece, belt pouches, painted prop, wig or styled hair
- Focus: one strong silhouette detail plus one signature accessory
- Tip: keep the prop lightweight so it survives a full convention day

## Day-by-Day Convention Schedule

### Day 1: Friday, 2026-07-10 — Arrival, check-in, and soft launch
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg
- Morning: Pack final costume pieces, chargers, tape, snacks, water bottles
- Afternoon: Arrive in Chicago, check in, steam/adjust costumes, test props
- Evening: Badge pickup, opening hall walk-through, low-key dinner, early night

### Day 2: Saturday, 2026-07-11 — Main cosplay day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/star.svg
- Morning: Dress in the more detailed cosplay, apply makeup/hair, leave extra time for photos
- Afternoon: Panels, dealer room, photo meetups, short rest break every 2-3 hours
- Evening: Casual street food or quick diner meal, costume touch-up, content sorting

### Day 3: Sunday, 2026-07-12 — Comfortable final day and departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: Wear the easy cosplay or a simplified version of the detailed look
- Afternoon: Final shopping, last photos, pack up before leaving the venue
- Evening: Transit home, unpack fragile items first, clean and store costume parts

## Packing Checklist for Two People

### Costumes and build supplies
- Main outfit pieces for both cosplays
- Backup shirt or base layer
- Wig, wig cap, hair ties, bobby pins
- Makeup, setting spray, wipes
- Safety pins, fashion tape, super glue, hot glue sticks
- Fabric scissors, small sewing kit, black thread
- Foam/prop materials, paint pen, touch-up markers

### Convention essentials
- Badge, ID, phone, charger, power bank
- Refillable water bottle
- Small crossbody bag or backpack
- Cash and card
- Pain reliever, bandages, blister pads
- Hand sanitizer, tissues, deodorant
- Sunglasses, compact umbrella or poncho

### Snacks for the weekend
- Granola bars
- Trail mix
- Fruit snacks or apples
- Sandwich wraps
- Electrolyte packets
- Gum or mints
- One “treat” item for morale

## Budget-Smart Tips for Chicago Transit and Food

- Use **CTA** for most rides if your hotel is near the convention area.
- Keep one **rideshare buffer** only for late-night or costume-heavy trips.
- Bring snacks from home or a grocery stop to avoid overpriced venue food.
- If the detailed cosplay gets expensive, shift money from props into the backup buffer.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Chicago Events & Travel](https://www.choosechicago.com/)
Action: [Button: Convention Checklist](https://www.google.com/search?q=convention+packing+checklist)

## Sources

- CTA trip planning: https://www.transitchicago.com/planatrip/
- Chicago travel info: https://www.choosechicago.com/
- General cosplay supply ideas: https://www.michaels.com/
